label: digit 3 input in the original phase at position >= 3
explanation: Fires when the input token is the digit 3 during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase at step t>=3. It is silent for a 3 at positions 0-1, nearly silent at position 2, silent on the delimiter, and essentially silent in the copy phase (162 stray steps), including when a 3 is fed back as input there. It does not fire on other tokens. Activation is larger when the 3 is late in the original sequence: top activations come from a 3 at t=5-6 right before <DEL> (to_go 0), while the weakest come from a 3 at t=3 with several tokens still to come. A first occurrence of 3 fires a bit more often than a repeat. Rate also goes up with the number of digits in the sequence.

issues: Test scores reproduce exactly: P 0.988, R 0.984, F1 0.986, mass recall 0.999.

All 687 test false positives are at t==3. Precision is 0.958 at t==3 and 1.000 at t>=4. Many of these steps come after a '1' earlier in the sequence. That is a small weak spot at the boundary, not a systematic class large enough to change the label.
The 922 missed activations are tiny (about 0.03-0.06 of max) and hold 0.1% of mass: stray copy-phase steps plus a few non-3 tokens. This is scattered noise.
The negative claims check out. A 3 at t==2 almost never fires (P 0.007), and a 3 fed back in the copy phase almost never fires (P 0.001). The delimiter never fires.
The magnitude claims match the profile. Activation mass rises with to_go toward 0, and the top examples are a 3 at t=5-6 just before <DEL>.

The claim that rate rises with n_digits is mostly a confound: the feature only fires on the digit 3, so sequences with more digits contain more 3s. It is mildly misleading but does not affect the label.
